summary: The window's own route to the device draws a page without its transfer functions. pdf_model carries them beside the display list as §11.7.5.2's channel (DisplayList::transfers) and pdf_render::resolve_transfers applies it, but only render-cpu's rasterize and render-raster's Rasterizer::rasterize call it. The window's present (render-raster present.rs, QuorraWindowRenderer::render -> FrameSlot::render -> scene_for, which viewer-device's renderer/device.rs draws every frame the device is asked for) translates the list's commands and never reads the channel, and nothing on viewer-device's or viewer-host's route sends such a page to the processor or refuses it (render-gpu refuses it by name; the window's backend neither applies nor refuses). A page filled red under /TR = 1 - x shows red in the window where rasterize of the same list shows cyan: by the same route issue6931_reduced.pdf's heart would be drawn black in the window (by reading; not run).
source: ISO 32000-2 §10.5: "In the sequence of steps for processing colours, the PDF processor shall apply the transfer function after performing any needed conversions between colour spaces." and "The output shall be the transformed component value to be transmitted to the device (after halftoning, if necessary)." §10.6.1: "Halftoning is not required for such devices; after gamma correction by the transfer functions, the colour components shall be transmitted directly to the device."

Hold both lanes with this test at every coverage.

summary: The window's own route draws §10.8.3's simulated press without its black ink. Under the reader's simulation the page composites on the simulated device and pdf_model hands the backends the process inks as two lists on one geometry: the complements of cyan, magenta and yellow on the list and black beside it (DisplayList::black, with blending()), plus any spot planes (separation()). rasterize draws the second list and multiplies the two back (pdf_render::resolve_blending / resolve_separation); the window's present translates the first list alone. A page filled 0 0 0 1 k under the simulation is [35, 31, 32] through rasterize and white [255, 255, 255] in the window's frame. By reading, the same route also drops a spot plane and a four-component page group's black list without the simulation (§11.4.7, outside this audit's clauses; the fix is the same).

source: ISO 32000-2 §10.5: "An RGB device shall use the first three, a monochrome device shall use the gray transfer function only, and a CMYK device shall use all four." "Transfer functions shall always operate in the native colour space of the output device, regardless of the colour space in which colours were originally specified." "If the component is subtractive (cyan, magenta, yellow, black, or a spot colour), it shall be converted to additive form by subtracting it from 1.0 before it is passed to the transfer function." §10.8.3 a): "Process the PDF as if separations were to be created for a simulated device that supports subtractive process colourants and possibly spot colours."

source: ISO 32000-2 §10.5: "When the current colour space is DeviceGray and the output device's native colour space is DeviceCMYK , a PDF processor shall use only the gray transfer function. summary: Stroke adjustment is applied only to a stroke under 1.5 device pixels (pdf_render::grid_fit::FIT_BELOW). The clause's first requirement binds every stroke /SA enables, and the tree's own reading of uniform thickness (ADR 2530: a whole number of pixel rows the same at every placement) is broken for a wider rule: two points wide centred at device y 49.75 it covers a quarter row, a row and three quarters of a row (3 rows) where the same rule on a pixel boundary covers 2. Rounding the width to whole pixels (within half a pixel) and moving the edges to pixel boundaries is the same construction at every width; ADR 2530 states the 1.5 bound as the construction's domain and gives no clause for it.
source: ISO 32000-2 §10.7.5: "When stroke adjustment is enabled, the line width and the coordinates of a stroke shall automatically be adjusted as necessary to produce lines of uniform thickness. The thickness shall be as near as possible to the requested line width -no more than half a pixel different." and "A line of a given width can intersect with different numbers of device pixels, depending on where it is positioned."
